summary.text: Coleman-Mach 48000-series rooftop air conditioners run on 115 VAC, 60 Hz, 1-phase power and are controlled from the ceiling assembly selector switch and rotary thermostat, or from a wall thermostat. R410A units protect the compressor with a High Pressure Switch lockout circuit.

models.text: Operation and maintenance instructions 1971AA982 cover 8000 series rooftop air conditioners and their ceiling plenums, designed for 115 VAC, 60 Hz, 1 phase power.
Model and serial numbers are on the I.D. label at the air conditioner basepan return air opening at the bottom of the roof unit, and on the rating plate.
The 46515 series is a two-ton packaged heat pump mounted below the floor, with two compressors on separate refrigeration circuits; its model and serial are on the unit rating plate.
9000 series units are designed for 240 volt electrical power.
473XX*XXX5 series units are 230/240 VAC, 1-phase, 50 Hz international 47000-series units; model and serial are on the unit data label.
Coleman-Mach cannot identify an AC from the RV VIN; it needs the model or serial number of the AC unit. Filters are set by the ceiling assembly, not the AC model.
Everest VS-18: ceiling assembly 2111-0044; wall thermostat 2111-0043 (heat/cool, controls an external furnace) or 2111-0045 (cool only).

display.text: 47000 remote-controlled units: the ceiling assembly has a two-color LED, red for heating and blue for cooling, beside the infrared receiver.
VS-18: press and hold the Turbo button 5 seconds to show the last main or sub error code recorded; the display shows 00 if there is none.
display.locator: 'How do I view stored fault codes on a VS-18 thermostat?'

display.text: VS-18 codes fall into E1-E9 (sensors, voltage, temperature, communication), H1/H2 (thermostat-drive signal), EA and dE/d2-dC (compressor drive faults).
display.locator: 'What causes communication or thermostat errors on the VS-18?'

reset.text: R410A units: after the High Pressure Switch trips, the compressor stays locked out until the 115 VAC supply power is turned off and back on to reset the circuit.
46515 packaged heat pump: the high pressure switch is a manual-reset push button in the unit electrical box; access is limited to qualified technicians, with 115 volt power off.
473XX electric heat: if dirty filters or restricted louvers stop the heat, turn power off at the mode selector switch, wait ten minutes and restore power; then correct the low airflow.
VS-18 fan stuck at low speed means the thermostat is in Sleep Mode (ECO held 5 seconds); press and hold ECO 5 seconds until the Sleep indicator goes out.
reset.locator: 'Why does my VS-18 appear to have only one fan speed?'

reset.text: If the remote is lost or malfunctions, the unit can be run from the two manual override buttons (heating and cooling) on the ceiling assembly.

checks.text: Domestic units need 115 VAC/60 Hz and may run safely between 105 and 125 volts; operating outside that range can seriously damage components.
Each air conditioner must be protected by a 20 amp time delay fuse or breaker; minimum wire size is #12 AWG for runs up to 25 feet.
Filters: release the two 1/4-turn fasteners and lower the ceiling grille, or remove four return grille screws on flush-mount assemblies; clean at least every two weeks of use.
Clean the outside (condenser) coil at least once a year: blow out debris, straighten bent fins, optionally rinse with water but never a pressure washer, with all power disconnected.
checks.locator: 'What type of maintenance does my RV air conditioner require?'

checks.text: Periodically check that roof mounting bolts are tight, the four shroud screws and washers are snug, and the shroud has no cracks or impact damage.

parts.text: The High Pressure Switch Safety Circuit trips on abnormal conditions such as fan motor failure, a dirty condenser coil or dirty filters.
Mach 8 freeze protection: the thermistor cuts out at 26 F (plus or minus 3) and resets at 40 F; the freeze switch on the condenser coil opens at 18 F coil temperature.

Mach 8 parts named: sealed hermetic compressor (not field serviceable), reversing valve solenoid, by-flow restrictor, overload switch, run and start capacitors, PTCR, heater limit switch; persons not qualified shall not service.
The motors are sealed and need no lubrication. The system is closed and sealed and should never need refrigerant recharging.

callTech.text: Anytime the air conditioner is not operating properly, a qualified technician should examine the power supply; all electrical work and inspection is for qualified service personnel only.
If breakers keep tripping, have an electrician check starting and running amperage; power normal but no fan or compressor points to the connector plug behind the ceiling control box.
Repeated High Pressure Switch lockouts mean the unit must be serviced by a qualified technician.
Suspected low refrigerant charge: have the unit evaluated by a qualified service technician.
callTech.locator: 'Do I need to check or add refrigerant?'

callTech.text: Do not break into the sealed refrigeration system unless properly trained in sealed system repairs.
VS-18: high voltage shock hazard; do not access the drive PCB on the rooftop unit.
